questions.q: Neoplasia is abnormal and rapid proliferation of cells / ↑ frequency of the ____.
questions.exp: ↑ frequency of cell cycle (Book p276)

questions.q: Match the anticancer class to its members.
right: Alkylating agents, platinum compounds, antitumor antibiotics
Anti-metabolites, topoisomerase I & II inhibitors, histone deacetylase blocker, hydroxyurea
Vinca alkaloids, taxanes, epothilones, eribulin, estramustine
More effective and less toxic; no effect on normal cell cycle
questions.exp: Non-CCS: alkylating/platinum/antitumor antibiotics; S-phase: anti-metabolites, topo I&II, HDAC blocker, hydroxyurea; M-phase: vinca, taxanes, epothilones, eribulin, estramustine; miscellaneous: more effective, less toxic (Book p276)

questions.q: The anti-metabolite subgroups listed under S-phase inhibitors are:
questions.exp: Anti-metabolites: anti-folates, pyrimidine analogs, purine analogs (Book p276)

questions.q: The histone ____ blocker is listed among S-phase inhibitors.
questions.exp: Histone deacetylase blocker (Book p276)

questions.q: The m/c dose-limiting toxicity of anticancer drugs is ____ suppression.
questions.exp: Bone marrow suppression: m/c dose limiting toxicity (Book p276)

questions.q: Match the proliferating normal tissue to its toxicity.
questions.exp: Bone marrow → suppression (DLT); hair follicles → alopecia; germ cells → infertility; GIT cells → mucositis/diarrhea (Book p276)

questions.q: Enterochromaffin-like cells cause drug-related nausea & vomiting via ↑5HT → (+)5HT3 and substance P → (+):
questions.exp: Substance P → (+) NK1; ↑5HT → (+)5HT3 → nausea & vomiting (m/c drug related S/E) (Book p277)

questions.q: Match the CINV grade to its setting and prevention.
right: Most drugs: anyone out of 1,2,3 (most preferred dexamethasone)
questions.exp: Severe (cisplatin) 4 drugs; moderate (carboplatin) 3 drugs; mild (most drugs) anyone, dexamethasone preferred (Book p277)

questions.q: In mild CINV the most preferred single agent is ____.
questions.exp: Most preferred: dexamethasone (Book p277)

questions.q: The 4th drug added for severe (cisplatin) CINV, beyond ondansetron/aprepitant/dexamethasone, is ____.
questions.exp: Severe: 1 ondansetron 2 aprepitant 3 dexamethasone 4 olanzepine (Book p277)

questions.q: Brain tumor: DOC is ____.
questions.exp: Brain tumor: temozolomide (Book p277)

questions.q: Head and neck carcinoma (oral): ____ ; alternate drug cetuximab.
questions.exp: Head and neck Ca (oral): cisplatin; alternate cetuximab (Book p277)

questions.q: Both esophageal and gastric carcinoma take ____ as their drug.
questions.exp: Esophageal Ca: cisplatin; gastric Ca: cisplatin (Book p277)

questions.q: Colorectal carcinoma: ____ (5FU); regimens add oxaliplatin + irinotecan + folinic acid (FOLFOX/FOLFIRI/FOLFIRINOX).
questions.exp: Colorectal Ca: 5 fluorouracil (Book p277)

questions.q: Anal carcinoma TOC regimen: 5FU + ____.
questions.exp: Regimen: 5FU + mitomycin-C (TOC) (Book p277)

questions.q: Urogenital carcinomas (bladder, uterine, ovary, testicular, cervical): DOC is ____.
questions.exp: Urogenital Ca: cisplatin (DOC) (Book p277)

questions.q: Prostate carcinoma: ____ [GnRH agonist (DOC)].
questions.exp: Prostate Ca: goserelin [GnRH agonist (DOC)] (Book p277)

questions.q: No response in urogenital carcinoma: add nivolumab and ____ (immune checkpoint inhibitors).
questions.exp: Add nivolumab, pembrolizumab — immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICP (-)) (Book p277)

questions.q: Retinoblastoma VEC regimen: vincristine + etoposide + ____.
questions.exp: VEC: vincristine + etoposide + carboplatin (Book p278)

questions.q: Lung carcinoma (SCLC & NSCLC) regimen: cisplatin + ____ ; no response → nivolumab + pembrolizumab.
questions.exp: Regimen: cisplatin + etoposide (Book p278)

questions.q: Hepatocellular carcinoma: DOC is ____.
questions.exp: Hepatocellular Ca: sorafenib (DOC) (Book p278)

questions.q: Pancreatic carcinoma regimen: ____.
questions.exp: Pancreatic Ca: FOLFIRINOX (Book p278)

questions.q: Malignant pheochromocytoma: vincristine + cyclophosphamide + ____.
questions.exp: Vincristine + cyclophosphamide + dacarbazine (Book p278)

questions.q: Renal cell carcinoma in this map is treated with ____.
questions.exp: Renal cell carcinoma: pembrolizumab (Book p278)

questions.q: Match the osteosarcoma MAP letters to the drugs.
questions.exp: MAP: methotrexate (high dose), adriamycin, platinum (cisplatin) + ifosfamide add-on (Book p278)

questions.q: Match the lung-cancer branch to its regimen.
questions.exp: Limited SCLC: cisplatin+etoposide; extensive: +pembrolizumab; NSCLC mutation(−): chemo + ICP inhibitor; double ICP: nivolumab+ipilimumab (Book p278)

questions.q: Keynote 189 trial: chemotherapy + ____.
questions.exp: Key note 189 trial: chemotherapy + pembrolizumab (Book p279)

questions.q: Match the EGFR-TKI generation to its drugs.
questions.exp: 1st gen gefitinib/erlotinib → T790M resistance; 2nd gen afatinib/dacomitinib ↑toxic; 3rd gen osmertinib for L858R (Book p279)

questions.q: Resistance to 1st-gen EGFR TKIs arises via the ____ mutation.
questions.exp: T790M mutation → resistance (Book p279)

questions.q: The 3rd-generation EGFR TKI used for the L858R mutation is ____.
questions.exp: Osmertinib; use: L858R mutation (Book p279)

questions.q: Match the ALK-inhibitor generation to its drugs.
questions.exp: Crizotinib → L1196; 2nd gen alectinib/brigatinib/ceritinib → G1202R resistance; 3rd gen lorlatinib (Book p279)

questions.q: Brigatinib is also used in the ____ mutation.
questions.exp: Brigatinib (also used in T790 mutation) (Book p279)

questions.q: Resistance to 2nd-gen ALK inhibitors is via the ____ mutation.
questions.exp: G1202R mutation → resistance (Book p279)

questions.q: ER-positive breast cancer: premenopausal gets ____ ; postmenopausal gets letrozole.
questions.exp: Premenopausal: tamoxifen; postmenopausal: letrozole (Book p279)

questions.q: No response to letrozole → ____ ; ESR-1 mutation → elacestrant.
questions.exp: No response → fulvestrant; elacestrant (ESR-1 mutation) (Book p279)

questions.q: Her2-positive breast cancer: DOC ____ ; resistance → neratinib, pertuzumab, lapatinib.
questions.exp: Trastuzumab (DOC); resistance → neratinib, pertuzumab, lapatinib (Book p279)

questions.q: Match the triple-negative breast cancer mnemonic DCP and BRCA drug.
questions.exp: DCP: doxorubicin, carboplatin, paclitaxel; add-on pembrolizumab; BRCA mutation: olaparib (Book p279)

questions.q: Match the leukemia to its regimen.
questions.exp: ALL VPAD; AML cytarabine + idarubicin/daunorubicin; CLL FCR (Book p280)

questions.q: AML with FLT-3 mutation adds ____ (FLT3 kinase inhibitor).
questions.exp: FLT-3 mutation → midostaurin (FLT3 kinase inhibitor) (Book p280)

questions.q: The 1st-generation BCR-ABL TKI that is DOC for CML & GIST is ____.
questions.exp: Imatinib (DOC): (CML & GIST) (Book p280)

questions.q: The 2nd-generation BCR-ABL inhibitors (enzymatic site) are:
questions.exp: 2nd generation: dasatinib, nilotinib, bosutinib — inhibit enzymatic site on tyrosine kinase (Book p280)

questions.q: The 3rd-generation BCR-ABL inhibitor after 2nd-gen no response is ____.
questions.exp: 3rd generation: ponatinib (Book p280)

questions.q: ____ inhibits the allosteric site on tyrosine kinase.
questions.exp: Asciminib: inhibit allosteric site on tyrosine kinase (Book p280)

questions.q: Omacetaxine inhibits the ____ protein; the book also lists TNF-α as a last option.
questions.exp: Omacetaxine: inhibits BCR-ABL protein (or) TNF-α (Book p280)

questions.q: Hodgkin's lymphoma ABVD: adriamycin, bleomycin, vinblastine and ____.
questions.exp: ABVD: adriamycin, bleomycin, vinblastine, dacarbazine (Book p280)

questions.q: No response in Hodgkin's lymphoma: nivolumab and ____.
questions.exp: No response → nivolumab, pembrolizumab (Book p280)

questions.q: Match the lymphoma type to its regimen.
right: R-CHOP: rituximab, cyclophosphamide, hydroxydaunorubicin, oncovin, prednisolone
questions.exp: Hodgkin's ABVD; low grade FCR; high grade R-CHOP (Book p280)

questions.q: Hairy cell leukemia: ____.
questions.exp: Hairy cell leukemia: cladribine (Book p280)

questions.q: Polycythemia vera, essential thrombocythemia and sickle cell disease share ____.
questions.exp: Hydroxyurea (Book p280)

questions.q: Multiple myeloma: bortezomib + lenalidomide + ____.
questions.exp: Bortezomib + lenalidomide + dexamethasone (Book p280)

questions.q: Match the side effect to the drug.
questions.exp: Vincristine → neurotoxicity (SIADH); cytarabine → cerebellar; cisplatin → oto/max N/V/nephro; bleomycin > busulfan → pulmonary fibrosis (Book p281)

questions.q: Cisplatin nephrotoxicity prevention: 1–2 ltr NS + mannitol (Cl-diuresis) + ____ (inactivates cisplatin).
questions.exp: A. 1–2 ltr NS B. mannitol C. amifostine — inactivate cisplatin (Book p281)

questions.q: Cardiotoxicity (doxorubicin, daunorubicin, trastuzumab): prevention for the anthracyclines is ____.
questions.exp: Prevention: dexrazoxane (Book p281)

questions.q: Hepatotoxicity: 6MP/6TG and ____ ; the latter can cause cirrhosis in rheumatic/psoriatic arthritis.
questions.exp: Hepatotoxicity: 6MP/6TG, methotrexate — cirrhosis in RA, psoriatic arthritis (Book p281)

questions.q: Diarrhea caused by irinotecan is treated with ____.
questions.exp: Diarrhea: irinotecan; treatment: loperamide (Book p281)

questions.q: Hemorrhagic cystitis (ifosfamide > cyclophosphamide) is prevented by ____.
questions.exp: Prevented: mesna (Book p281)

questions.q: Hand and foot syndrome (capecitabine > 5FU) is prevented with vitamin ____ supplement.
questions.exp: Prevention: vit B6 supplement (Book p281)

questions.q: Bone marrow suppression (pemetrexed > methotrexate): prevention is folinic/folic acid + vitamin ____ injection (for pemetrexed).
questions.exp: Folinic acid (leucovorin)/folic acid + vit B12 inj (for pemetrexed) (Book p281)

questions.q: Flagellate dermatitis is caused by ____.
questions.exp: Flagellate dermatitis: bleomycin (Book p281)

units.title: Neoplasia and Classification
units.guide: Neoplasia = rapid proliferation/↑ cell-cycle frequency. Non-CCS: alkylating, platinum, antitumor antibiotics. CCS S-phase: anti-metabolites (anti-folates, pyrimidine, purine), topo I&II, HDAC blocker, hydroxyurea. M-phase: vinca, taxanes, epothilones, eribulin, estramustine. Misc: more effective/less toxic. DLT bone marrow; alopecia; infertility; mucositis.

units.title: CINV and Its Prevention
units.guide: ECL cells: ↑5HT→5HT3, substance P→NK1 → N/V (m/c S/E). Severe (cisplatin): ondansetron+aprepitant+dexamethasone+olanzepine; moderate (carboplatin): first 3; mild (most drugs): anyone, dexamethasone preferred.

units.title: Drug of Choice in Carcinoma 1
units.sec: Drug of Choice in Carcinoma 1 · p277
units.guide: Brain temozolomide; head & neck cisplatin (alt cetuximab); esophagus/gastric cisplatin; colorectal 5FU (FOLFOX/FOLFIRI/FOLFIRINOX); anal 5FU+mitomycin-C (TOC); urogenital cisplatin (±nivolumab/pembrolizumab); prostate goserelin (GnRH agonist DOC).

units.title: Drug of Choice in Carcinoma 2
units.sec: Drug of Choice in Carcinoma 2 · p278
units.guide: Retinoblastoma VEC; lung cisplatin+etoposide (→ nivolumab+pembrolizumab); HCC sorafenib; pancreatic FOLFIRINOX; pheochromocytoma vincristine+cyclophosphamide+dacarbazine; RCC pembrolizumab; osteosarcoma MAP + ifosfamide.

units.title: Lung Cancer Details
units.guide: SCLC limited: cisplatin+etoposide; extensive: +pembrolizumab. NSCLC mutation(−): chemo + pembrolizumab/atezolizumab or double ICP nivolumab+ipilimumab; Keynote 189: chemo + pembrolizumab.

units.title: NSCLC Mutations and Breast Cancer
units.sec: NSCLC Mutations and Breast Cancer · p279
units.guide: EGFR: 1st gen gefitinib/erlotinib (T790M resistance) → 2nd gen afatinib/dacomitinib (↑toxic) → 3rd gen osmertinib (L858R). ALK: crizotinib (L1196) → alectinib/brigatinib (also T790)/ceritinib (G1202R) → lorlatinib. Breast: ER+ tamoxifen/letrozole→fulvestrant/elacestrant (ESR-1); Her2 trastuzumab→neratinib/pertuzumab/lapatinib; triple-negative DCP + pembrolizumab; BRCA olaparib.

units.title: Hematological Malignancy: Leukemia
units.guide: ALL VPAD; AML cytarabine + idarubicin/daunorubicin (FLT-3 → midostaurin); CLL FCR. CML: imatinib (DOC, CML & GIST) → 2nd gen dasatinib/nilotinib/bosutinib (enzymatic site) → ponatinib → asciminib (allosteric), omacetaxine (BCR-ABL protein), TNF-α.

units.title: Lymphoma and Others
units.guide: Hodgkin's ABVD (→ nivolumab/pembrolizumab). NHL low grade FCR; high grade R-CHOP. Hairy cell: cladribine. PV/ET/sickle: hydroxyurea. Myeloma: bortezomib + lenalidomide + dexamethasone.

units.title: Organ-Specific Side Effects
units.guide: Vincristine neuro (SIADH); cytarabine cerebellar; cisplatin oto/N/V/nephro (NS+mannitol+amifostine); bleomycin>busulfan pulmonary fibrosis + flagellate dermatitis; doxorubicin/daunorubicin cardio (dexrazoxane); MTX/6MP hepato; irinotecan diarrhea (loperamide); ifosfamide hemorrhagic cystitis (mesna); capecitabine hand-foot (B6); pemetrexed marrow (folinic+B12).
